key_results: Mach-disk width is more NPR-sensitive than height and transient dimensions overshoot semi-steady values.
Hydrogen/methane differ in pre-disk mixing and shock dimensions at matched NPR.
Hydrogen penetration is nonmonotonic with NPR in the studied geometry.

mechanisms.summary: NPR and gas properties set shock geometry; shear/turbulence then sets mixing location and jet development.

evidence_candidates.claim: Mach-disk height and width increase strongly with NPR, but the transient values overshoot their semi-steady values and therefore state qualification is essential.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Table 3 gives case-specific semi-steady dimensions; Fig. 7 documents early overshoot and formation/stabilization chronology.
evidence_candidates.limitations: LES, one nozzle geometry, ambient conditions below many engine conditions.

evidence_candidates.claim: At matched NPR=8.5, hydrogen and methane differ in Mach-disk geometry and pre-disk mixing; the authors attribute hydrogen pre-disk mixing to stronger nozzle-exit turbulence and Gortler vortices.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Matched-gas cases quantify disk geometry and show mixing-location differences.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Attribution is model-based and gas-property effects are coupled.

evidence_candidates.claim: Increasing NPR did not monotonically increase hydrogen jet penetration in this geometry.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: After the initial transient, NPR 70 approached NPR 8.5 penetration and NPR 30 was about 8% lower.
evidence_candidates.limitations: The proposed optimum near NPR 100 is explicitly tentative and geometry-specific.
